messages.author: d35e483a32894a6c
messages.subject: Error in installing RStan
parts:
Hi, guys,

I want to install rstan into my laptop. I follow the instructions on RStan homepage. However, this error always appears: 

Error in assign(".popath", popath, .BaseNamespaceEnv) : 
  cannot change value of locked binding for '.popath'
Calls: local ... eval.parent -> eval -> eval -> eval -> eval -> assign
Execution halted

The downloaded source packages are in
        ‘C:\Users\ISUSunny\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpkNNpq7\downloaded_packages’
Error in library(rstan) : there is no package called ‘rstan’
In addition: Warning messages:
1: running command '"C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-31~1.1/bin/x64/R" CMD INSTALL -l "C:\Users\ISUSunny\Documents\R\win-library\3.1" C:\Users\ISUSunny\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpkNNpq7/downloaded_packages/Rcpp_0.11.5.tar.gz' had status 1 
2: In install.packages("Rcpp", type = "source") :
  installation of package ‘Rcpp’ had non-zero exit status
3: package ‘inline’ was built under R version 3.1.3 
4: package ‘Rcpp’ was built under R version 3.1.2 
5: running command '"C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-31~1.1/bin/x64/R" CMD INSTALL -l "C:\Users\ISUSunny\Documents\R\win-library\3.1" C:\Users\ISUSunny\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpkNNpq7/downloaded_packages/rstan_2.6.0.tar.gz' had status 1 
6: In install.packages("rstan", type = "source") :
  installation of package ‘rstan’ had non-zero exit status

I have no idea why this happened. My laptop uses the Windows OS. I have installed the RTools. My R Release and RStudio are the latest. 

Does anyone have some ideas about this? 
Thanks,﻿
Sunny

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Error in installing RStan
parts:
On Sunday, April 19, 2015 at 4:40:48 PM UTC-4, Chenhui Liu wrote:
installation of package ‘Rcpp’ had non-zero exit status

This is not (yet) a problem with RStan but rather Rcpp, which RStan depends on. Try to install Rcpp from source and see why it fails.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Error in installing RStan
parts:
On Sunday, April 19, 2015 at 8:58:40 PM UTC-4, Chenhui Liu wrote:
Do you have any idea about this error?

No. There is a chance, albeit a small one, that you could compile Stan models if you had the binary Windows Rcpp package installed. However, it is recommended to install Rcpp from source in order to prevent issues from arising when your setup is different than CRAN's. In any event, you should ask the Rcpp list about this problem.

Ben
